title: Maple Hollow Rising Revisited
premise: Ivo Eriksen has spent five years in Maple Hollow rebuilding after a fire took her grandfather's lighthouse and her confidence with it, writing anonymous letters to a stranger as therapy. When the letter recipient, Wren Calloway, moves next door to restore the abandoned vineyard, the decade-long correspondence is exposed, forcing both women to confront what they hid between the lines. As the vineyard's first harvest approaches, Ivo must forgive herself for the fire she believes she caused, and Wren must choose between the safe life she left and the one being written beside her. They end the season together at the harvest festival, co-authoring a new life instead of trading letters across a distance that no longer exists.
about_author: Astrid Quintana is the pen name of a former lighthouse archivist who spent seven years cataloguing coastal correspondence before turning to fiction. She writes quiet romances about people who rebuild, and lives within sight of the sea.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Five years after the fire, Ivo tends the rebuilt lighthouse lamp and drafts another unsent letter, number one hundred and twelve. Establishes her careful, measured life and the guilt she carries. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Sold to the Highest Bidder
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Calloway arrives in Maple Hollow having bought the derelict Halvorsen vineyard sight unseen, fleeing a corporate career and an engagement she broke off. She knows the town only through letters signed 'I.' Emotional beat: reckless hope.

chapters.title: Next Door
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo discovers her new neighbor is renovating the vineyard cottage — and recognizes Wren's handwriting on moving boxes: she is the letter recipient. Panic; Ivo hides the connection. Emotional beat: terror of exposure.

chapters.title: Borrowed Sugar, Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren knocks on Ivo's door for help with a burst pipe. Their chemistry is immediate but Ivo deflects. Wren mentions, casually, the letters that got her through her darkest year. Emotional beat: near-miss intimacy.

chapters.title: Rows of Dead Vines
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Wren asks Ivo's grandfather's old friend, vintner Marta, to assess the vines; Ivo tags along and is pulled into the restoration despite herself. First laughter shared. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ivo's POV. The night of the fire five years ago: Ivo fell asleep with a candle while writing letters, or so she believes. Her grandfather's death and the town's unspoken blame. Emotional beat: the wound beneath everything.

chapters.title: The Letters in the Attic
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sorting the cottage attic, Wren finds a crate of undelivered replies from Ivo's grandfather to his late wife — proof the letter habit runs in the family. She begins to suspect who 'I' is. Emotional beat: dawning recognition.

chapters.title: Harvest Is a Promise
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Marta declares the vines salvageable if the first harvest happens this fall. The whole town mobilizes; Ivo is drafted as record-keeper, trapping her in proximity to Wren. Emotional beat: community as pressure and balm.

chapters.title: Rain on Tin Roofs
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A storm traps Wren and Ivo in the barn overnight. Walls come down; almost-kiss interrupted by a call from Wren's ex-fiancé. Emotional beat: desire meeting old obligation.

chapters.title: The Ex Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Wren's ex-fiancé Daniel shows up to win her back, charming the town instantly. Ivo retreats into self-sabotage, convinced she ruins everything she touches. Emotional beat: jealousy sharpened by unworthiness.

chapters.title: Number One Hundred and Twelve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds Ivo's latest unsent letter blown into the vineyard rows — and finally confirms Ivo wrote every letter. She says nothing, hurt that Ivo hid it. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: Cold Cellar, Colder Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo realizes Wren knows. They circle each other through harvest prep, all business, no warmth. Marta warns Ivo that unforgiven things ferment badly. Emotional beat: the cost of secrets.

chapters.title: Daniel's Proposal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Daniel proposes publicly at the town diner, staging a grand gesture. Wren refuses him in front of everyone — then turns to find Ivo watching, and can't read her face. Emotional beat: liberation shadowed by doubt.

chapters.title: The Mirror in the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Alone in the lamp room, Ivo confronts the truth: the fire started from faulty wiring, not her candle — her grandfather knew and never told her to spare her. Grief and rage at being protected into guilt. Emotional beat: the first crack of self-forgiveness.

chapters.title: Marta's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Marta reveals she found the fire marshal's report years ago and stayed silent out of loyalty to Ivo's grandfather. Wren carries the truth back to Ivo. Emotional beat: inherited silence broken.

chapters.title: What We Wrote Between the Lines
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ivo and Wren finally speak plainly — reading their letters aloud to each other in the cellar among the barrels. Every hidden feeling laid bare. They kiss as rain ends a dry spell. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. An early frost threatens the entire first harvest. The town works through the night; Ivo leads, stepping fully back into the community that once blamed her. Emotional beat: redemption through action.

chapters.title: The Old Flame Question
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Daniel returns one last time with a job offer in the city. Wren chooses Maple Hollow definitively — but Ivo, spooked by happiness, pushes her away first. Emotional beat: fear wearing armor.

chapters.title: Empty Chair at the Table
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Harvest eve dinner without Wren. Ivo reads letter one hundred and thirteen aloud to her grandfather's memory, admitting she wants a life, not just safety. Emotional beat: choosing courage over the wound.

chapters.title: First Pressing
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Harvest day. Ivo arrives at the vineyard at dawn and asks Wren to stay — not as neighbors, but as partners. The grapes go to press; so do their defenses. Emotional beat: vulnerability answered.

chapters.title: Maple Hollow Rising
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The harvest festival: the first vintage poured, the lighthouse relit in honor of Ivo's grandfather, the town's blame formally dissolved in toast and tears. Emotional beat: communal healing.

chapters.title: Chapter One, Together
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Epilogue in spring: Ivo finishes her novel — dedicated to 'the person behind the letters' — and Wren plants new vines. They write one final letter and hand-deliver it, same door, no distance. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed into beginning.
